headline: Q1/Q2: hardening streaming, auth/transport, and tool-calling across the provider matrix
body:
Three independent, roughly equal-sized (effort 8) workstreams are queued: streaming reliability (Q1), enterprise auth/transport (Q1), and tool-calling pipeline hardening (Q2). None block each other (depends_on: nothing for all three), but they touch overlapping surface area — httpx client config, provider-specific message/SSE handling, and agent/graph execution paths — so sequencing and cross-review matter even without hard dependencies.

Streaming work covers six distinct fixes: tolerating SSE payloads that omit the 'event:' field (e.g. Anthropic via Bedrock proxy) instead of hard-failing with zero generation chunks; fixing spurious Pydantic serializer warnings and dropped response metadata/headers (x-request-id) when combining with_structured_output with streaming; fixing disable_streaming='tool_calling', which currently crashes with an AttributeError (AsyncStream passed where ChatCompletion is expected) and, even when it doesn't crash, disables streaming globally instead of scoping to tool-calling turns; routing agent/graph internal LLM calls through astream instead of ainvoke so on_llm_new_token actually fires when graph-level streaming is enabled; plus test-infra work (standard test coverage/release sequencing for tool-call streaming across integration packages, including unsupported ones like Mistral) and correcting a known-bad assertion in the core streaming error-callback test that currently masks whether error-path behavior is correct.

Auth/transport work adds custom httpx client and mTLS support to ChatAnthropic (for corporate proxy/PKI setups), fixes MCP tool discovery so configured auth headers/tokens are reliably forwarded (eliminating spurious 403s), migrates AzureChatOpenAI/BaseChatOpenAI toward a shared httpx client/connection-pooling layer to remove redundant connection/auth setup, and closes an SSRF/allowlist bypass where environment-based auth checks let requests reach untrusted hosts. The SSRF fix is flagged high-risk for breaking legitimate configs that currently rely on environment-based auth to reach internal hosts — needs careful scoping.

Tool-calling (Q2) is the largest surface: provider-specific validation relief for injected tool-call history (Gemini thought-signature/turn-order rules), graceful handling of malformed/fragmented streamed tool-call payloads instead of crashes or silent misexecution, making tool_choice respect model capabilities (not force 'required' on reasoning models that only support 'auto'/'none'), closing the gap where ToolNode can execute a human-rejected tool call, adding tool_call_id to on_tool_start/on_tool_end events for parallel-call attribution, proactive warning before tool-call limits are hit, and unifying handle_tool_error/ToolException behavior across @tool, ToolNode, and wrap_tool_call middleware. The HITL rejection-enforcement fix is safety-critical — an incomplete fix could give false confidence that rejected calls are blocked.
call_to_action: Review the SSRF/allowlist change and the disable_streaming='tool_calling' scoping change for backward-compat risk before implementation — both are flagged as potentially breaking existing behavior — and flag if you see sequencing conflicts with the Q2 tool-calling work given the shared httpx client refactor touches provider integrations also affected by streaming's astream routing changes.
